statement: An Entity that is told how a payment passes through it acts on it by itself, as frames of its Accounts: a hub that holds a lock for a hashlock it has a forward entry for locks the same amount and hashlock on the next hop with a deadline one hop (reserve plus lag) sooner, passes the secret to the lock it came in on when the next hop shows it, in a frame it takes, or on the chain, or in a frame it refuses as frozen (R-DISPUTE-FREEZE; a frame refused for any other fault shows nothing), and gives that lock up when the next hop gives its own up or its Account refuses the lock; a lock too near its deadline for another hop is given up, not forwarded. A payee with an entry resolves a lock for the token and at least the amount it asked, and gives any other up. An entry belongs to one hashlock and one peer: only that peer's lock is forwarded, and a second entry for a hashlock is refused. Owed: a next hop that never answers (expiry and the on-chain reveal of a hub that learned the secret), entries that outlive a payment, and the fee a hub would take. An entry comes from a command or from the route a lock names (R-LOCK-ROUTE): the first hop of the route is the next hop and the rest goes on the next lock; an entry told to the hub stands over a route; a route through a peer the hub has no Account with, back to the sender, or over the limit is given up or refused.
source: consolidation-plan.md e2e rows 4 and 5 (deadlines chain by HOP plus window; a downstream failure reaches A); R-HTLC-CLOCK; R-ONE-LOCK-PER-HASH; testnet-e2e step S5 (gap htlc-route)

killers.name: R-HTLC-FORWARD a lock made to the hub is forwarded and resolved back to Alice
R-HTLC-FORWARD the next hop's lock is one hop sooner and carries the same amount and hashlock
R-HTLC-FORWARD a payee asked for more than the lock holds gives it up and the hub gives up Alice's
R-HTLC-FORWARD a lock too near its deadline for another hop is given up, not forwarded
R-HTLC-FORWARD a payee that was asked for another token gives the lock up
R-HTLC-FORWARD a lock the next hop's Account refuses is told and given up upstream
R-HTLC-FORWARD one next hop giving its lock up fails only the payment that went to it
R-HTLC-FORWARD an entry forwards only a lock of the peer it names
R-HTLC-FORWARD a second entry for one hashlock is refused and the first stands
R-HTLC-FORWARD a payment with no hop to forward to waits and moves nothing
R-HTLC-FORWARD a lock that names its route is forwarded with no entry told to the hub
R-HTLC-FORWARD each hop of a route forwards to the next with the rest of the route
R-HTLC-FORWARD a route through a peer the hub has no Account with is given up, and the lock with it
R-HTLC-FORWARD a route back to the peer the lock came from is given up
R-HTLC-FORWARD an entry told to the hub stands over the route a lock names
R-HTLC-FORWARD a route longer than the limit makes the lock refused at the door
R-HTLC-FORWARD two payments to one next hop in one frame take two slots and both go through
R-HTLC-FORWARD with lag 1 and reserve 2 a lock due at 110 is forwarded due at 107
R-HTLC-FORWARD at view 100 a lock due at 104 is forwarded due at 101 and one due at 103 is given up
R-HTLC-FORWARD a next hop that already holds a lock gets a slot above it
R-HTLC-FORWARD a lock the hub itself made to the peer is not an incoming lock to forward
R-HTLC-FORWARD a secret shown by the next hop is passed up, by any other peer it is not
R-HTLC-FORWARD a secret shown for an entry that has locked nothing yet is not passed up
R-HTLC-FORWARD a cancel fails the entry of its own token and slot, not the first entry to that peer
R-HTLC-FORWARD a resolve in a frame accepted over the hub's own pending frame is learned and passed up
R-HTLC-FORWARD a resolve in a frame that is refused leaves the entry locked and nothing passed up
